title: An Autopatch deployment ring does not approve drivers automatically

report.title: {Items.Count} Autopatch {Plural(Items.Count, 'ring waits', 'rings wait')} for a driver approval by hand

messages.businessImpact: Driver and firmware updates wait for somebody to approve them one at a time. In practice nobody does, so devices sit on old firmware, and the fixes that matter most, for storage, power and security hardware, are the ones that go uninstalled.
messages.technicalDetail: Each Autopatch deployment ring has its own driver update policy, and the approval choice belongs to the policy rather than to the group. A ring left on manual approval defers nothing: it offers nothing at all until an approval is added.
remediation: Set driver and firmware approvals to automatic on the deployment rings, so each ring receives drivers on its own schedule.
Keep manual approval only where a ring exists to hold a specific driver back, and review that queue on a named day.
messages.cannotSee: Rings are read from the names of the driver update policies Autopatch creates, so a renamed policy is not matched. How long an approval has been waiting is a separate collection this release does not make, so the finding says the ring waits rather than how much is queued behind it.
